ai.literal: Virtue, wealth, pleasure, life-fear: of the four, the nature having examined, [one] will be trusted.
ai.translation: A person should be trusted only after examining their true nature against four tests: virtue, wealth, pleasure, and fear for their life.
ai.modern: அறம், பொருள், இன்பம், உயிருக்கு ஆபத்து வரும்போது ஏற்படும் அச்சம் ஆகிய நான்கு நிலைகளிலும் ஒருவனது இயல்பை ஆராய்ந்த பிறகே அவனைத் தேர்ந்தெடுக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the four fundamental tests for evaluating a person's character before trusting them with responsibility. The tests are based on how they react to the demands of virtue, the lure of wealth, the temptation of pleasure, and the fear of losing their life. By examining their true nature (திறம்) under these four pressures, a leader can confidently choose the right person. The compound 'உயிரச்சம்' (fear for life) specifically highlights the ultimate test of loyalty and courage when facing mortal danger.

ai.literal: Family having-been-born, from-fault having-been-freed, blemish shrinking-from sense-of-shame he-who-possesses pointing-indeed trust.
ai.translation: Trust should be placed in a man born of a good family, free from faults, and possessing a sense of shame that shrinks from any blemish.
ai.modern: நல்ல குடியில் பிறந்து, குற்றங்களிலிருந்து நீங்கி, பழிக்கு அஞ்சும் நாணத்தை உடையவனையே தேர்ந்தெடுத்து நம்ப வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the qualities of a person worthy of trust and responsibility. The person must come from a respectable family ('குடி') and be free from flaws ('குற்றத்தின் நீங்கி'). Furthermore, they must possess a deep sense of shame ('நாண்') that makes them shrink from any moral blemish ('வடு'). The word 'சுட்டு' indicates that the choice or direction of one's trust ('தெளிவு') should point exclusively to such an individual.

ai.literal: Rare things having learned, those who are without fault even with, when examining, absence is rare indeed of ignorance.
ai.translation: Even among those who have learned difficult subjects and are free from faults, when examined closely, a complete absence of ignorance is rare indeed.
ai.modern: அரிய நூல்களைக் கற்று குற்றமற்றவர்களாக இருப்பவர்களிடத்திலும், ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்தால் அறியாமை சிறிதும் இல்லாமல் இருப்பது மிகவும் அரிது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns that no one is entirely perfect when choosing people for tasks. Even individuals who have mastered difficult subjects and appear completely faultless will have some minor flaws or areas of ignorance. The word 'வெளிறு' refers to ignorance or a blank spot in one's understanding. Therefore, a leader must carefully examine candidates and accept that a total absence of weakness is practically impossible to find.

ai.literal: Good quality having examined, and fault having examined, among them excess having examined, the abundant take.
ai.translation: Examine a person's good qualities and examine their faults; then, weighing which is greater, judge them by that majority.
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய நல்ல குணங்களையும் ஆராய்ந்து, அவருடைய குற்றங்களையும் ஆராய்ந்து, அவற்றுள் எவை அதிகமாக இருக்கின்றன என்று பார்த்து, அந்த மிகுதியானவற்றைக் கொண்டு அவரைப் பற்றி முடிவு செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: To evaluate a person for a task or trust, one must objectively examine both their virtues and their flaws. Since no one is entirely perfect or entirely flawed, the decision should be based on the balance of these traits. By weighing which side is greater, one can accept and judge the person according to their predominant qualities.

ai.literal: For greatness and other smallness, their respective deeds indeed are the touchstone.
ai.translation: A person's own deeds are the touchstone that tests their greatness and their smallness.
ai.modern: ஒருவரின் பெருமைக்கும் சிறுமைக்கும் உரைகல்லாக அமைவது அவரவர் செய்யும் செயல்களே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how to judge a person's true worth. It uses the metaphor of a touchstone, which is a dark stone used to test the purity of gold. Just as the stone reveals the quality of the metal, a person's own actions reveal whether they are great or small. Therefore, one should evaluate others based entirely on what they do.

ai.literal: Those who are destitute (acc.) trusting let one avoid; for they, attachment they are without, they will not be ashamed of blame.
ai.translation: Avoid trusting those who are destitute and without ties. Since they have no attachments, they will not be ashamed of incurring blame.
ai.modern: எந்தப் பற்றுக்கோடும் இல்லாதவர்களை நம்பி ஒரு பொறுப்பை ஒப்படைப்பதைத் தவிர்க்க வேண்டும். ஏனென்றால், அவர்கள் சமூகத்தின் மீதோ நற்பெயரின் மீதோ பற்று இல்லாதவர்கள் என்பதால், பழிச்சொல்லுக்கு வெட்கப்பட மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises against placing trust in people who have nothing to lose. The word 'aṟṟār' can mean those who are financially destitute or those who lack social and moral ties; in the context of choosing whom to trust, it refers to those without roots or standing. Because such people have no meaningful attachments ('paṟṟu') to society, family, or reputation, they do not fear the consequences of their actions. Consequently, they will not feel ashamed of committing faults or facing public blame ('paḻi').

ai.literal: Affection as support, knowledge those who know not trusting, folly all will give.
ai.translation: Trusting those who lack knowledge, relying solely on one's affection for them, will result in every kind of folly.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாதவர்களை அவர்கள் மீதான அன்பை மட்டுமே பற்றுக்கோடாகக் கொண்டு நம்பித் தேர்ந்தெடுப்பது, எல்லாவிதமான அறியாமையையும் குற்றங்களையும் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against letting personal affection override objective evaluation when choosing people for tasks. 'காதன்மை' means affection or attachment, and 'கந்து' refers to a support or peg. Using affection as the sole support ('கந்தா') to trust ('தேறுதல்') those who lack the necessary knowledge ('அறிவு அறியார்') is a grave mistake. Such a choice will only result in complete folly ('பேதைமை எல்லாம் தரும்'), leading to failure and ruin.

ai.literal: He who does not examine, a stranger, he who trusted - lineage, unending sorrow will give.
ai.translation: Trusting a stranger without testing him will bring unending sorrow to one's descendants.
ai.modern: ஒருவனைப் பற்றி ஆராயாமல் முன்பின் தெரியாதவனை நம்பி ஒரு செயலை ஒப்படைத்தவனுக்கு, அது அவனது தலைமுறைக்கும் நீங்காத துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against placing trust in unknown people without proper investigation. The word 'தேரான்' means failing to examine, and 'பிறனை' refers to someone who is an outsider or stranger. 'தெளிந்தான்' denotes the one who places his trust or confidence. The phrase 'வழிமுறை' indicates that the consequences of such a careless decision will not stop with the individual, but will pass down to their lineage. Thus, the text emphasizes that blind trust yields 'தீரா இடும்பை' or sorrow that never ends.

ai.literal: Do not trust anyone without examining; after having examined, entrust the task to be entrusted.
ai.translation: Do not place your trust in anyone without testing them first. Once you have tested them, entrust them with the tasks they are fit to handle.
ai.modern: யாரையும் ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்காமல் நம்பிவிடக் கூடாது; நன்றாக ஆராய்ந்த பிறகு, அவர் செய்வதற்கு ஏற்ற செயலை அவரிடம் ஒப்படைக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of careful evaluation before delegating responsibilities. The word 'தேராது' means without examining, and 'தேறற்க' means do not trust, setting a strict rule against blind faith in anyone. Once a person is thoroughly tested ('தேர்ந்த பின்'), one should confidently entrust ('தேறுக') them with the specific tasks ('தேறும் பொருள்') they are qualified to perform. The repetition of the roots 'தேர்' (to examine) and 'தேறு' (to trust) creates a strong contrast between the process of selection and the act of delegation.

ai.literal: Without examining, trust, and in one who was trusted, suspicion, unending sorrow will give.
ai.translation: Trusting someone without prior examination, and doubting someone after having trusted them, will both cause unending sorrow.
ai.modern: ஒருவரை ஆராயாமல் நம்புவதும், நன்கு ஆராய்ந்து நம்பிய பின் அவரிடம் சந்தேகம் கொள்வதும் தீராத துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet warns about two critical mistakes in choosing and trusting people. The first is placing trust in someone without thoroughly examining their character and capacity. The second is harboring suspicions about someone after they have been tested and chosen. Both of these actions are flawed and will yield unending sorrow, because the former leads to betrayal and the latter destroys a good working relationship.
